extra.message: The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as the string literal 'Keep it secret, keep it safe'. This key signs all Flask session cookies, so anyone with access to the source can forge valid session cookies for any user, including an admin session (_user_id=1), completely bypassing authentication (app/models/models.py:20 defines is_admin as username=='admin').

app.config['DEBUG'] = True enables Flask/Werkzeug debug mode in the application configuration. When the app is run via app.run() (line 96) or manage.py runserver, the Werkzeug interactive debugger is active: unhandled exceptions (e.g., the AttributeError in api/views.py:25 when a message id is not found) expose full stack traces, source code, and local variables, and the debugger console permits arbitrary Python code execution on the server.

Stored XSS: message content is rendered with the Jinja2 '| safe' filter, which disables HTML auto-escaping. The content is user-controlled from two sources: (1) the unauthenticated API endpoint MessagesView.post (app/blueprints/api/views.py:43-56) which stores request.get_json()['message'] verbatim, and (2) the authenticated feedback form (app/blueprints/account_area/views.py:66,75) which stores request.form['feedback']. When an admin views the Messages panel, attacker-supplied JavaScript executes in the admin's browser session, enabling session hijacking and admin account takeover.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Stored XSS: the message author (from_user) is rendered with the '| safe' filter, disabling auto-escaping. from_user is fully attacker-controlled: the unauthenticated API endpoint MessagesView.post (app/blueprints/api/views.py:50-52) copies data.get('from_user') from the request JSON directly into the Message record with no validation, also allowing author impersonation (e.g., from_user='admin'). A crafted from_user value such as '' executes in the admin's browser when viewing the Messages panel.

extra.message: Reflected XSS: the 'name' GET parameter is rendered with the Jinja2 '| safe' filter, which disables HTML auto-escaping. The value comes directly from request.args.get('name', 'world!') in app/blueprints/sandboxes/views.py:13 with no sanitization. An attacker can craft a link like /sandbox/unsafe_params?name=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script> that executes arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser when clicked.

extra.message: Reflected XSS: the 'name' value is rendered with the Jinja2 '| safe' filter, which disables HTML auto-escaping. The value originates from the user-controlled cookie request.cookies.get('name') (app/blueprints/sandboxes/views.py:27) or POST form field request.form.get('name') (app/blueprints/sandboxes/views.py:28). An attacker can set a cookie 'name=' or submit the form to execute arbitrary JavaScript when the page renders.

extra.message: MessagesView.post() creates database records without any authentication or authorization check, unlike the sibling methods index/get/delete/acknowledge_message which are all decorated with @admin_required. Any unauthenticated attacker can POST JSON to this endpoint with arbitrary 'message' and 'from_user' values (lines 47-52), which are then rendered unescaped to administrators in app/templates/admin/message.html:29-30. This enables unauthenticated stored XSS against admins and author impersonation.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Open redirect: the 'next' query parameter is read from the request (request.args.get('next', url_for('index'))) and passed directly to Flask's redirect() with no validation or allowlist. An attacker can craft a link like /toggle_xss_protection/?next=https://evil.com to redirect users to a malicious site for phishing. This endpoint is linked from the navbar form on every page (app/templates/_base.html:66-67).

cwe: CWE-601: Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: User passwords are stored in a plain db.String(200) column with no hashing or salting. The User constructor (lines 14-17) stores the raw password, and the login view compares it directly with plaintext equality (app/blueprints/login/views.py:17: 'user.password == password'). Anyone with database access (e.g., via the world-readable sqlite file at /tmp/test.db configured in app/flask_xss.py:24) obtains every user's password in cleartext.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: The User.serialize property includes the plaintext password ('password': self.password). This serialized dict is returned by the API endpoint UsersView.index (app/blueprints/api/views.py:72) via jsonify, so a GET to /api/v1/UsersView/ dumps every user's cleartext password. Combined with the hardcoded SECRET_KEY (app/flask_xss.py:23) allowing trivial admin session forgery, this enables a full credential dump.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The /account_area/change_email endpoint is a state-changing POST handler protected only by cookie-based session authentication (@login_required). No CSRF token is generated or validated anywhere in the application (no Flask-WTF, no token in the forms.html macros), and the Flask 0.12 session cookie is set without a SameSite attribute. An attacker can host a page with an auto-submitting form POSTing a new email to this endpoint; when a logged-in victim visits it, their account email is changed without consent (update at lines 54-57).

The /account_area/send_feedback endpoint is a state-changing POST handler protected only by cookie-based session authentication with no CSRF token validation. An attacker can forge a cross-site form submission that creates Message records in the victim's name (lines 75-77, from_user=current_user.username); because those messages are rendered unescaped in the admin panel (app/templates/admin/message.html:29-30), this also provides a CSRF-to-stored-XSS delivery path.

The login page displays the message 'Use credentials "admin/admin" to log in as admin' to every unauthenticated visitor, disclosing the default administrator credentials. Combined with the default password in manage.py (add_admin(password='admin')) and the is_admin check based solely on username=='admin' (app/models/models.py:20-21), any visitor can immediately gain full administrative access.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The add_admin management command defaults the administrator password to the hardcoded value 'admin' (def add_admin(password='admin')). If the command is run without an explicit password argument, the admin account is created with these well-known default credentials, which are additionally disclosed on the login page (app/blueprints/login/templates/login/login.html:5).

The after_request handler explicitly sets the response header 'X-XSS-Protection: 0' whenever the session toggle is disabled (the default state), instructing browsers to turn off their built-in XSS auditor for every response. This disables a defense-in-depth mechanism and increases the impact of the multiple XSS vulnerabilities in the application. No Content-Security-Policy header is set anywhere either.

The SQLAlchemy database URI is 'sqlite:////tmp/test.db', placing the application database in the shared, world-readable /tmp directory. Since the database stores passwords in plaintext (app/models/models.py:11) and sqlite creates files with default permissions (typically 0644), any local user or process on the host can read the entire user table including usernames, passwords, and emails.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: print('New admin credentials are admin/{}'.format(password)) writes the plaintext administrator password to stdout when the admin account is created. In containerized or CI/CD deployments where stdout is captured by log aggregation, the admin password persists in log storage visible to anyone with log access.
